study type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
exposure: Timing of intrauterine copper device (IUCD) insertion (immediate postpartum vaginal, intra-caesarean, delayed postpartum, interval)
Maternal characteristics (age, socioeconomic status, education, occupation, parity)
Timing of IUCD insertion (immediate postpartum vaginal, intra-caesarean, delayed postpartum, interval)
outcome: Proportion of patients unable to feel IUCD thread
cohort: 1631 eligible mothers who received IUCD insertion at a tertiary-care center in India between July 2013 and July 2014
finding: Immediate postpartum insertion of an intrauterine copper device (IUCD) was the safest and most efficacious time for insertion, with the lowest expulsion rate, highest continuation rate, and no failures.
mod_finding: Intra-caesarean IUCD insertion had a lower expulsion rate than immediate postpartum vaginal insertion but a higher rate of patients unable to feel the IUCD thread.
